chunks: My father (peace be upon him) said: Sa'd ibn Abd Allah narrated to me from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn Sayf from his brother Al-Husayn ibn Sayf ibn Amirah from Mansur ibn Hazim who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying:
One who passes a single day in which he prays fifty prayers but does not recite 'Qul Huwa Allahu Ahad' in any of them, it will be said to him: O servant of Allah, you are not of those who pray.

key_terms.أَبَا عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ع: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), a title for Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq.
key_terms.خَمْسِینَ صَلَاهً: Fifty prayers, indicating a high volume of ritual prayer.
key_terms.قُلْ هُوَ اللَّهُ أَحَدٌ: Surah Ikhlas (The Sincerity), a short chapter of the Quran emphasizing divine unity.

ai.seo_question: What is the consequence of praying without reciting Surah Ikhlas?
ai.summary: In *Thawab al-Amal*, Shaykh al-Saduq records this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) to emphasize that mere quantity of prayer is insufficient without the core declaration of monotheism, Surah Ikhlas. The Imam’s rebuke, 'you are not of those who pray,' signifies a spiritual disqualification rather than a mechanical invalidation, highlighting the centrality of Tawhid in Shia jurisprudence and devotion. This serves as a critical reminder for believers to ensure the essential recitation is not omitted even in voluntary or numerous prayers.

en.sayed-athar-husain-rizvi-&-sayed-maqs: 1.  It is narrated that Imam Ja’far Sadiq (a.s.) said, “One who offers all of the five prayers of a day without reciting Surah Ikhlaas in any of them, will be told: O servant of Allah! You are not of those who pray.”
